types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalObject: A celestial body or structure, such as a star, planet, galaxy, or black hole. Also called celestial body, cosmic entity, space object, heavenly body. Examples: black hole star, red dots, star, black hole.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalObject
chosen_type.definition: A celestial body or structure, such as a star, planet, galaxy, or black hole.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents celestial bodies; existing candidates are for media or intangible concepts. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.

candidates.label: TextObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a text file, which can contain unformatted text or markup like HTML. Also called text file object, digital text file, document media. Examples: a plain text file (.txt), an HTML file, a Markdown document. Distinct from TextDigitalDocument, which is a structured digital document primarily composed of text.

candidates.label: AlignmentObject
candidates.comment: An AlignmentObject is an Intangible item describing a relationship or correspondence between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Also called learning alignment, competency mapping, educational standard link. Examples: A resource aligned to a specific Common Core State Standard, a course module mapped to a learning outcome, a textbook chapter linked to a curriculum objective.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called idea, notion, abstract, principle. Examples: mystery, energy, energy source, number one.

chosen_type.label: Concept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or general notion.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general abstract concept; existing candidates are too specific or too broad (Thing). Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: MolecularEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.

types.embedding_query_text: CosmicRegion: A specific area or domain within the universe. Also called space region, celestial domain, cosmic area. Examples: early universe, universe's infancy, Galactic centers.

chosen_type.label: CosmicRegion
chosen_type.definition: A specific area or domain within the universe.
chosen_type.justification: Existing schema.org 'Place' subtypes are too specific to Earth's geography. Minting a new type with Place as parent, as it's the closest general concept for a region.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalSystem: A group of celestial bodies and structures that are gravitationally bound. Also called star system, planetary system, galaxy system. Examples: solar system.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalSystem
chosen_type.definition: A group of celestial bodies and structures that are gravitationally bound.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents astronomical systems; existing candidates are for biological, software, or classification systems. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: AnatomicalSystem
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

types.embedding_query_text: TimePeriod: A duration or interval of time. Also called epoch, era, span, duration. Examples: 660 million years after the Big Bang.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Duration' class accurately represents a period or interval of time, matching the OIE type and example.

mentions: 660 million years after the Big Bang

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

types.embedding_query_text: CosmicEvent: A significant occurrence or phenomenon in the history of the universe. Also called cosmic phenomenon, universal event, celestial occurrence. Examples: Big Bang.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Event' class is the most general and appropriate type for a significant occurrence like the 'Big Bang'.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchTeam: A group of individuals collaborating on a scientific investigation or project. Also called research group, scientific team, study group. Examples: U.S.-led team of astronomers, team of astronomers, team, research team.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: A 'ResearchOrganization' is an organization dedicated to research, which closely aligns with the concept of a 'ResearchTeam' of astronomers.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: Telescope: An optical instrument designed to make distant objects appear nearer, containing an arrangement of lenses or of curved mirrors and lenses, by which rays of light are collected and focused in a way that forms a magnified image. Also called observatory instrument, optical device, astronomical instrument. Examples: James Webb Space Telescope, JWST, Webb telescope, Webb.

chosen_type.label: Telescope
chosen_type.definition: An optical instrument designed to make distant objects appear nearer, containing an arrangement of lenses or of curved mirrors and lenses, by which rays of light are collected and focused in a way that forms a magnified image.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an optical instrument like a telescope; existing candidates are irrelevant. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: Optician
candidates.comment: An Optician is a local business that sells reading glasses and similar devices for improving vision. Also called optical store, eyewear shop, optometrist's office (if selling glasses). Examples: LensCrafters, a local independent optician, an online glasses retailer. Distinct from Ophthalmologist, who is a medical doctor specializing in eye care.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

types.embedding_query_text: Publication: A document or work made public, such as an article, book, or report. Also called published work, document, report, article. Examples: study.

chosen_type.label: ScholarlyArticle
chosen_type.justification: A 'study' is often a formal article presenting research, making 'ScholarlyArticle' a good specific fit for the general 'Publication' type.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: PublicationEvent
candidates.comment: A PublicationEvent is an Event corresponding to the publication of a CreativeWork, regardless of its type or delivery medium. Also called release event, publishing event. Examples: the release of a new book, the broadcast of a TV show, the online publication of an article, the launch of a new album.

types.embedding_query_text: Journal: A periodical publication containing articles on a particular subject. Also called academic journal, periodical, magazine. Examples: Nature.

chosen_type.label: Periodical
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Periodical' class perfectly describes a publication issued in successive parts, such as a journal like 'Nature'.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: Newspaper
candidates.comment: A Newspaper, as a Periodical, is a publication containing information about varied topics, often published daily. Also called daily paper, news publication, gazette. Examples: The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, a local community newspaper. Distinct from Magazine, which is typically published weekly or monthly with a specific focus.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: MedicalScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A scholarly article specifically within the medical domain. Also called medical journal article, clinical research paper, healthcare publication. Examples: a peer-reviewed article on a new drug, a research paper on surgical techniques, a review article on a disease. Distinct from ScholarlyArticle, which is a broader category for academic papers.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day of the year. Also called calendar day, day, specific date. Examples: Wednesday, Tuesday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The mentions 'Wednesday' and 'Tuesday' are specific days of the week, which directly match the schema.org 'DayOfWeek' enumeration.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1. Also called calendar year, annum. Examples: 2022.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Date' data type can represent a specific calendar date, including a year like '2022'.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A paid occupation, especially one that involves prolonged training and a formal qualification. Also called occupation, career, vocation, calling. Examples: scientists.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.definition: The control of a country or region by a foreign military power.
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Occupation' class directly matches the definition of a 'Profession' and applies to 'scientists'.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called individual, human, individual. Examples: Rohan Naidu, Robert Simcoe, Florian Peißker.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Person' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and mentions of individual human beings.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education and research which grants academic degrees. Also called college, academy, educational institution. Examples: University of Hawaii, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, University of Cologne.

chosen_type.label: CollegeOrUniversity
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'CollegeOrUniversity' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and mentions of higher education institutions.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: HighSchool
candidates.comment: A HighSchool is an educational organization and civic structure providing secondary education. Also called secondary school, senior high, academy. Examples: Springfield High School, Northwood Academy, a local public high school.

types.embedding_query_text: Communication: The imparting or exchanging of information by speaking, writing, or using some other medium. Also called message, announcement, statement, discourse. Examples: statement.

chosen_type.label: Statement
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Statement' class, defined as a declaration or assertion, is a direct match for the OIE type 'Communication' when exemplified by 'statement'.

candidates.label: CommunicateAction
candidates.comment: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: InformAction
candidates.comment: An InformAction is a communicate action representing the act of notifying someone of pertinent information without expecting a response. Also called notify action, announce action, advise action. Examples: sending a broadcast email, posting a public announcement, informing a colleague about a meeting change. Distinct from AskAction, which seeks information, and ReplyAction, which responds to communication.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

types.embedding_query_text: DataProduct: Information, especially facts or numbers, collected to be examined and considered, and used to help decision-making, or information produced by a system. Also called dataset, information product, output data. Examples: images, data, new observations, Webb’s mid-infrared data.

chosen_type.label: Dataset
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Dataset' class, representing a structured collection of information or data, is an excellent fit for 'DataProduct' and mentions like 'images' and 'data'.

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: DataCatalog
candidates.comment: A DataCatalog is a collection or repository of datasets, often providing metadata and access information for each. Also called data repository, dataset collection, data portal. Examples: A government open data portal, a university research data catalog, a scientific data archive.

candidates.label: DataFeed
candidates.comment: A DataFeed is a continuous stream or single file of structured information, typically updated regularly, about one or more entities or topics. Also called RSS feed, Atom feed, data stream, information feed. Examples: A news RSS feed, a stock market data feed, a product inventory feed, a weather data API.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

types.embedding_query_text: CosmicMaterial: Any substance or matter found in space or celestial bodies. Also called space matter, celestial substance, cosmic substance. Examples: dust, hydrogen gas, cocoon of gas, oxygen-rich dust.

chosen_type.label: Substance
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Substance' class, representing any matter of defined composition, is a good general fit for 'CosmicMaterial' and mentions like 'dust' and 'gas'.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: MolecularEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

types.embedding_query_text: AtmosphericPhenomenon: An observable event or occurrence in the Earth's atmosphere. Also called weather event, atmospheric event, meteorological phenomenon. Examples: wildfire smoke.

chosen_type.label: AtmosphericPhenomenon
chosen_type.definition: An observable event or occurrence in the Earth's atmosphere.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a natural phenomenon like 'wildfire smoke'; existing event types are too specific. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: OnDemandEvent
candidates.comment: An OnDemandEvent, as a PublicationEvent, is a publication event where a program is available on-demand. Also called catch-up TV, podcast release, streaming event. Examples: a TV show episode available for streaming after broadcast, a podcast episode release, a movie available for rent online. Distinct from BroadcastEvent, which is a live or scheduled transmission.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory. Also called nation, state, land. Examples: Canada, Germany.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Country' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and mentions of nations.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.embedding_query_text: AtmosphericRegion: A specific area or layer within a planet's atmosphere. Also called sky region, air space. Examples: sky.

chosen_type.label: AtmosphericRegion
chosen_type.definition: A specific area or layer within a planet's atmosphere.
chosen_type.justification: Existing schema.org 'Place' subtypes are too specific to Earth's landforms; 'sky' is an atmospheric region. Minting a new type with Place as parent.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Mountain
candidates.comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: Volcano
candidates.comment: A landform, typically a mountain, with a vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are ejected. Also called active volcano, dormant volcano, volcanic mountain. Examples: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Kilauea.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large town. Also called metropolis, urban area, municipality. Examples: Boston.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'City' class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and mention of a large town.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: Property: An attribute, quality, or characteristic of something. Also called characteristic, attribute, quality, feature. Examples: intrinsic color, wavelengths.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Property' class directly matches the definition of an attribute or characteristic, fitting 'intrinsic color' and 'wavelengths'.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: PropertyValueSpecification
candidates.comment: A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition. Examples: a specification for the allowed range of a numerical property, a definition of valid input for a text field, a schema for a complex property value.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: ElectromagneticRadiation: Energy that is propagated through space in the form of electromagnetic waves. Also called radiation, light, electromagnetic wave. Examples: light, pure black hole star light, infrared light.

chosen_type.label: ElectromagneticRadiation
chosen_type.definition: Energy that is propagated through space in the form of electromagnetic waves.
chosen_type.justification: While 'light' is energy, schema.org 'Energy' is a Quantity. No class represents the phenomenon or type of electromagnetic radiation. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: RadiationTherapy
candidates.comment: RadiationTherapy is a MedicalTherapy using radiation to improve a health condition. Also called radiotherapy, radiation treatment. Examples: radiation for cancer treatment, targeted radiation therapy, external beam radiation, brachytherapy.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration indicating whether a product is EnergyStar certified. Also called Energy Star rating, Energy Star certification. Examples: EnergyStarCertified, NotEnergyStarCertified.

candidates.label: BroadcastFrequencySpecification
candidates.comment: A BroadcastFrequencySpecification is an Intangible entity detailing the frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService. Also called frequency details, broadcast parameters, channel specification. Examples: 99.5 FM, 1080 AM, UHF channel 23.

candidates.label: RadioBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A RadioBroadcastService is a BroadcastService delivering radio content via broadcast over the air or online. Also called radio service, broadcast radio. Examples: BBC Radio 4, NPR, a local FM radio station, an internet radio stream.

types.embedding_query_text: Process: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end. Also called procedure, operation, method, course. Examples: nuclear fusion, creation of future stars, dust production.

chosen_type.label: Process
chosen_type.definition: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general 'Process'; existing candidates are specific actions. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: CreateAction
candidates.comment: A CreateAction is the act of deliberately producing, generating, or building a new result or entity by an agent. Also called production, generation, fabrication, construction. Examples: Writing a book, composing a song, building a house, designing a website.

candidates.label: CookAction
candidates.comment: The act of preparing or producing food through cooking processes. Also called cooking, food preparation, culinary action, baking. Examples: Baking a cake, frying an egg, grilling a steak, boiling pasta. Distinct from CreateAction, which is a broader category for making something.

candidates.label: PlanAction
candidates.comment: PlanAction is an OrganizeAction that involves arranging the execution of an event, task, action, reservation, or plan for a future time. Also called scheduling, arranging, pre-arranging. Examples: planning a wedding, scheduling a meeting, arranging a trip itinerary, setting up a project timeline.

candidates.label: AchieveAction
candidates.comment: AchieveAction is an instantaneous Action representing the accomplishment of something through prior efforts. Also called accomplish, attain, succeed, complete. Examples: Winning a race, graduating from college, reaching a sales target, completing a project.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

types.embedding_query_text: Methodology: A system of methods used in a particular area of study or activity. Also called approach, technique, procedure, method. Examples: modeling simulations.

chosen_type.label: Methodology
chosen_type.definition: A system of methods used in a particular area of study or activity.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a general 'Methodology'; 'MeasurementMethodEnum' is too specific. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: HowToSection
candidates.comment: A HowToSection is a creative work representing a sub-grouping of steps within a larger HowTo guide. Also called instruction chapter, procedural segment, how-to module. Examples: 'Preparing the Dough' in a bread recipe, 'Connecting the Wires' in an electronics manual.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

types.embedding_query_text: Symbol: A mark or character used as a conventional representation of an object, function, or process. Also called sign, emblem, representation. Examples: BH and asterisk.

chosen_type.label: DefinedTerm
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'DefinedTerm' class represents a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, which fits a 'Symbol' like 'BH and asterisk'.

candidates.label: Brand
candidates.comment: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: Drawing
candidates.comment: A Drawing is a CreativeWork that is a picture or diagram made with a pencil, pen, or crayon, as opposed to paint. Also called sketch, illustration, diagram, rendering. Examples: A charcoal portrait, a pen-and-ink landscape, a technical blueprint, a child's crayon drawing.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

types.embedding_query_text: Environment: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates. Also called surroundings, habitat, setting. Examples: extreme environment, harsh conditions, surroundings.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Place' class is the most general and appropriate fit for 'Environment' as it represents a physical setting or location.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

types.embedding_query_text: ObservationType: A category or method of perceiving or recording information. Also called observation method, viewing type, detection mode. Examples: mid-infrared view, clear signature.

chosen_type.label: ObservationType
chosen_type.definition: A category or method of perceiving or recording information.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org 'Observation' is an instance, not a type or method of observation. No suitable candidate exists. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: PurchaseType
candidates.comment: PurchaseType is an Enumeration listing different types of purchases for an item. Also called buying type, acquisition method. Examples: outright purchase, subscription, rental, lease.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: ViewAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming or perceiving static visual content. Also called look at, observe, gaze upon. Examples: viewing a photograph, looking at a painting, examining a diagram.

candidates.label: TrackAction
candidates.comment: The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing. Examples: tracking a package delivery, monitoring a flight's progress, tracking a lost phone.

types.embedding_query_text: Distance: The extent of space between two objects or points. Also called length, separation, gap. Examples: 0.55 light-years.

chosen_type.label: Distance
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Distance' class, representing a numerical value with a unit of length, is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and mention.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalFeature: A distinct part or characteristic of an astronomical object or region. Also called celestial feature, cosmic characteristic. Examples: star's surrounding envelope, dust envelope.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalFeature
chosen_type.definition: A distinct and observable characteristic or part of a celestial body or astronomical system.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents astronomical features; existing candidates are for Earth's geography or accommodations. Minting a new type with Thing as parent.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: GeoShape
candidates.comment: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.
